721510102.text: Sorry, I got a little distracted...

721510103.text: You guys are... unfamiliar faces. Sorry...I'm not very good at talking to strangers.

721510104.text: Ah... sorry... I didn't mean to be rude, I'm just... Sorry...

721510106.text: Paimon's name is Paimon, nice to meet you!

721510108.text: Sorry, I just... rarely chat with people.

721510109.text: May I ask... Is there anything I can help you with?

721510111.text: We were just wondering, what animal carcass is this...?

721510113.text: Her name is Kuntira, she's sort of... my childhood friend.

721510116.text: This might sound silly... You may even think it's just my wishful thinking...

721510117.text: This skeleton is what my childhood friend left behind.

721510120.text: Your friend was able to defeat such a huge sea creature... That's amazing!

721510124.text: I mean, these are the bones of my childhood friend. She's a sea creature.

721510126.text: On Narukami Island — my father's hometown, people call these creatures "Umibouzu"...

721510127.text: It is also said that they often attack cargo ships on long voyages and will rob fishermen of their catch... So they are hunted down and killed by humans.

721510128.text: But over here — my mother's hometown — the locals would give each individual creature a unique name.

721510129.text: And she, my best friend... may have been the last of her kind.

721510132.text: The people of Watatsumi never gave her species a common name.

721510133.text: Because they think that... Just like us, each of them is a lonely individual.

721510134.text: Lonely, docile, indifferent to curiosity and hostility outside of their own world...

721510135.text: Alone, roaming in the currents. Alone, suffocating in the shallows.

721510138.text: Don't think of it that way.

721510139.text: Intentionally or not, when you say words like "how pitiful," you're alienating yourself from the other person and their experience. It dismisses and trivializes their pain.

721510140.text: Only by empathizing with the other party's loneliness and pain, letting go of fear and defense, can we truly achieve understanding...

721510141.text: Perhaps that was why we happened to become friends back then.

721510142.text: Rather than alleviating each other's loneliness, we were enjoying the loneliness together, a solitude we both shared.

721510143.text: It's just that I have been away for a long time since I grew up. I finally had the opportunity to come back, only to realize that it's too late...

721510202.text: ...Ah, sorry, I didn't expect you guys to be back so soon.

721510208.text: Thank you for your hard work, it's good to take a break here.

721510301.text: Thank you so much! I knew I could count on you guys!

721510302.text: ...Mm, these are enough to make a wreath of flowers, thank you once again.

721510303.text: By the way... I have one more thing I want to ask of you, I don't know if you guys mind...

721510304.text: Since we've already helped you out, feel free to tell us, Miss Kumi!

721510307.text: ...It's like this. I heard from the elders of Bourou Village that there is hilichurl activity again on the beach to the west.

721510308.text: It so happens that a researcher from Sumeru passed by here the other day and is heading there... I think her name is Anisa, and she hasn't returned yet.

721510310.text: That researcher... Is she your friend?

721510311.text: Are friends the only ones worth worrying about?

721510312.text: Sorry, I mean... I don't really know her well, but I'm just worried.

subQuests.subQuestName: Head to the hilichurl camp in the west

721510401.text: *panting* Phew... Thank you, if it weren't for your help, I'm afraid I would be dead...

721510403.text: You're Anisa, right? Miss Kumi asked us to come!

721510404.text: Kumi...? Oh! It's that...local lass who looks a bit gloomy but is very nice, right?

721510406.text: What a strange and flippant way of describing her...

721510407.text: Hehe... Actually, I forgot her name. I really shouldn't have. I'll have to thank her properly later on.

721510408.text: Oh, yes, her name is "Kumi," right?

721510409.text: That's right! You shouldn't be a researcher with a memory like that!

721510410.text: Yes, I remember this time! Kumi, that's a cute name. Kumi...

721510412.text: Ah, sorry, I didn't introduce myself, although you might already know...

721510413.text: I'm Anisa. Anisa Purbiruni. Trainee Dastur at Sumeru Akademiya's Oceanographic Society.

721510414.text: As for my surname, Purbiruni, it's because my academic lineage dates back five centuries to the great scholar, the sage Biruni.

721510415.text: Ah, every time I mention this, a pride that cannot be expressed in words wells up within me unbidden!

721510416.text: Man, she's like some rich girl bragging about her dad's money...

721510420.text: Nothing... I'm just a little embarrassed about making people worry about me...

721510421.text: Paimon's surprised that you can be embarrassed at all!

721510422.text: However, there are still things that I have yet to do. The research I have on hand has not yet borne fruit, and so I must hurry.

721510423.text: You know, the statues of Watatsumi here are the object of my research. The traditional beliefs of the people of Watatsumi are very fascinating.

721510425.text: In antiquity, the priests... uh, I mean, shrine maidens of Watatsumi would place permanently-given offerings under memorials.

721510426.text: After that, they would protect those offerings with sophisticated mechanical puzzles or simple elemental techniques.

721510428.text: This was originally a manner of protecting and storing objects that were offered...

721510429.text: But people gradually discovered the joys of solving puzzles for their own sake, and even considered this a way of communicating with the now-deceased through one's intellect.

721510430.text: As such, the solving of puzzles became melded together with religious rituals, resulting in a most unique tradition.

721510431.text: As such, apart from the usual offerings, "solving puzzles left by those who came before" and seeking the "desires of the heart" also became rituals of worship or divination.

721510432.text: Of course, the better part of this is my personal guesswork. If we want to be sure, we'll need to conduct a great deal of folklore studies.

721510433.text: So, these "desires of the heart" are actually...

721510434.text: It's as you've guessed. I'm referring to the riches offered to the statues of Watatsumi — the gifts of forebears to their descendants.

721510436.text: By which I mean treasure, of course — treasure!

721510438.text: Your little companion seems to have a strong interest in my topic of study. How about it, then? Interested in lending me a hand?

721510441.text: Come on, there's treasure! Let's just help out, shall we?

721510442.text: As for me, I'm not all that interested in treasure. I just need my research results.

721510443.text: It'll be great if you're willing to help. The treasure's all yours. Consider it your payment for helping me out!

721510501.text: Hello there. Thanks for bringing Anisa back safe and sound.

721510504.text: Hello there, Little... uh, Miss Kumi. Sorry for making you worry.

721510505.text: I'm just glad to see that you're all right. I've just finished my garland, too.

721510506.text: Sorry for taking up your time. Let me give her this garland...

721510509.text: I hope that my feelings, though late, will get through to her.

721510513.text: Eh, why are you suddenly asking that?

721510515.text: I hear that the people of Watatsumi give each individual a unique name.

721510516.text: If you don't mind me asking, what was your friend's name?

721510520.text: The elders on the island say that "kuntira" means "whale" in the ancient language.

721510521.text: But I chose this name because I like it...

721510522.text: Well, it also fits with "Kumi," doesn't it? It's a lovely name!

721510526.text: *cough* Apologies. I spoke a little out of turn.

721510528.text: She was the last remnant of their kind. She was born alone, and she died alone.

721510529.text: Born in the sea, dying on land where she didn't belong, suffocating in the air...

721510530.text: Recently I've been thinking, sooner or later, this might be my destiny as well.

721510535.text: There's no need to persuade me... I understand what you're thinking... but after all, you and I are not the same...

721510536.text: I wasn't born here, nor do I belong to my father's hometown...

721510537.text: No, I was talking about the pelvic bones.

721510541.text: Pelvic bones? What are you talking about?

721510543.text: Have you guys noticed, that unlike a whale, she still has well-developed pelvic bones.?

721510544.text: Not at all... How did you notice?

721510545.text: Since I first arrived here, I have been paying attention to its pelvic structure... and the traces it left behind. I suppose you can call this an academic's instinct, hehe.

721510546.text: Hmmm...for example, when we give birth, we experience strong expansions and contractions, and as such, a stable support structure that protects our internal organs and soft tissues is indispensable.

721510547.text: Our pelvis is the structure that performs this function, and for Kuntira, her pelvis is the same.

721510551.text: A pelvis that has undergone childbirth tends to show a certain degree of deformation and wear due to expansion and contraction.

721510552.text: The body shape of primitive marine creatures tends to be teardrop-shaped, so their pelvises are also narrower.

721510553.text: In other words, the marks of pelvic deformation are more obvious and easier to observe.

721510557.text: Ah, sorry, I've just been talking about common knowledge. I suppose I've been boring you all to death.

721510559.text: You have a very beautiful tone of voice, at least. Has anyone ever told you that?

721510560.text: Uhm... Thank you... I never noticed... *cough* *cough* Um, thanks.

721510561.text: Ahem... Back to the topic at hand... As such, I have grounds to fully refute your reasoning.

721510562.text: Based on the deformations of the pelvic bones, she must have undergone many births. It seems she had found her home in the sea, and...

721510563.text: She had more than one offspring...

721510565.text: Hmmm, in other words, she found her own happiness.

721510566.text: But if that's the case...then why would she...

721510569.text: Haha, that's your second mistake, Miss Kumi.

721510570.text: Stranded sea animals often show signs of distortion and strain on certain parts of their vertebrae.

721510571.text: If you must know why, it's because suffocating is... very painful.

721510573.text: But based on my preliminary observations, Kuntira's spine is straight, almost as if she did not experience any painful struggle...

721510574.text: Based on a rough observation of her bone age, I would estimate that she passed away safely before she came to shore...

721510575.text: As for why she came to this familiar place in her final hours...

721510576.text: Maybe this was her way of telling her good friend that she had lived a happy and fulfilling life.

721510579.text: So, you've got to live well, too.

721510582.text: ...You know, I would always feel torn as to whether I should return to my home on Narukami Island or to stay here in Bourou Village...

721510583.text: Before, I was also torn whether to head back to Akademiya or stay in this country.

721510584.text: Due to the war, confusion, the pressure from the Shogunate...it's all too much, and many people have considered giving up.

721510585.text: But one must make a choice, to continue or to give up. Choosing to continue may still wind up being fruitless, but choosing to give up...

721510587.text: When it's war or government, they're just another problem. This is another matter entirely...

721510589.text: Think about it, hundreds of years later when people talk about this war, they can only lament the tragedy it caused and how meaningless it all was.

721510590.text: But when they talk about the history of Watatsumi Island, about your friends, and you and me, they will remember...

721510591.text: That this island had a daredevil that stumbled out and somehow unlocked some of the truths behind our history?

721510592.text: Yes, and that there also lived a girl who befriended a giant sea creature, and thus decided where her home should be.

721510594.text: When she was young, when she first met me, I had a similar feeling... the feeling that my life was only just beginning.

721510595.text: Then let your life begin once again — this time, without any fear of loss.

721510596.text: (Ohh, Paimon's getting mad! We were running all these errands for them, and here they are, chatting away!)

subQuests.subQuestName: Solve the puzzle of the Watatsumi statue

721510701.text: Well then, congratulations are in order!

721510704.text: Haha, it's fine. It's like I said, this is a symbol of "the heart's desire."

721510705.text: The forebears of this land left it to those who came after, as a symbol of faith and a token of trust. In fact, hmm, you could consider it a concrete way of "passing memories on."

721510706.text: So be at ease and just take it. It's yours by right.

721510707.text: The people of Watatsumi understood this very early on: the fruits of wisdom are to be given to those who respect it.

721510710.text: Of course! Thanks for your hard work!

721510712.text: Ah, no need to be so formal!

721510713.text: *sigh* Still, this thesis I'm working on is such a headache.

721510714.text: Eh? Didn't you have a breakthrough already?

721510715.text: Well, yes. But I've spent far too much time on just one subject.

721510716.text: To formally become a Dastur as opposed to remaining a trainee, you need to have two different theses pass through the review stage...

721510717.text: I can ask for an extension, of course, but I do still need to find a second topic.

721510718.text: My second field of study is actually marine biology, but due to the recent instability in Inazuma, I've had to call a halt to research on that front.

721510901.text: Can I help you with anything?

721510903.text: She's a researcher from Sumeru. She's rather reckless, but she has a beautiful voice...

721510904.text: She said that her field of study was Oceanic Sanctuary Storage... something. I'm not sure what that's about, really.

721510905.text: But she seems to be very interested in that Watatsumi statue on the beach to the west...

721510907.text: Mm-hmm. The village elder used to say that if we could solve the shrine maiden's puzzle, then "our heart's desire" would emerge.

721510908.text: Hehe, I used to believe that. Everyday, I would swim near that statue... That was actually how I met my good friend as well.

721510909.text: But I grew out of that a long time ago. I no longer believe in those stories.

721510910.text: Still, I can't help but feel happy for Anisa — that she still has so much interest and passion regarding these old legends.

721510911.text: I hope that she finds what she seeks...

721510912.text: Well, but before that, please find out if she's alright. Thank you very much.

721511001.text: Ah, it's you. Is there anything else I can help you with?

721511003.text: Oh, thank you. How is she?

721511006.text: Mmm, as long as she's alright... She can be really reckless, and it's very worrying.

721511007.text: I know that we're still practically strangers, but I wouldn't want to see anyone get hurt needlessly, especially at times like these...

721511101.text: It's fine if you can't solve it for now. The puzzle isn't going to run away or anything!

721511102.text: I'll be here too — so just relax.
